outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a read of the public data and news above, meant to help you decide, not a recommendation. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.reason: ASML raised its full-year 2026 revenue outlook for the second time this year, to €43B-€45B from €36B-€40B, on AI-driven demand — one of the few chip names higher today even as the broader memory-chip complex sold off.

strongest.area: Enterprise software rebound (Salesforce, ServiceNow) and cybersecurity's relative strength
strongest.reason: Salesforce and ServiceNow both bounced today after Morgan Stanley's downgrade-driven drop earlier in the week, while cybersecurity names like Palo Alto Networks continue to hold up better than the broader enterprise-software group on a relative basis.

weakest.area: Memory chips & AI hardware supply chain
weakest.reason: An overnight KOSPI selloff led by SK Hynix and Samsung dragged U.S. memory names sharply lower — Micron fell nearly 7% and SanDisk around 8-9% — while Arm dropped 8% despite record quarterly earnings, as management flagged smartphone-chip supply constraints and held off raising guidance.

The Nasdaq closed its third straight losing session as investors kept scrutinizing the size of AI-capex guidance versus near-term returns; Oracle extended its slide, now down roughly 9% over two sessions, still working through the same capex-return debate weighing on cloud peers.

outlook.nextStep: ASML's second guidance raise this year and the Salesforce/ServiceNow bounce look like the more durable, multi-day signals worth a closer look; the Korea-led memory rout and Arm's post-earnings drop are sharper, single-catalyst moves better watched for confirmation before drawing conclusions, especially with Teradyne's July 28 earnings and the Fed's July 28-29 meeting both still ahead.

signals.title: Fed rate-hike odds climb sharply ahead of the July 28-29 meeting
signals.body: CME FedWatch data shows the market-implied odds of a 25-basis-point hike at the July 28-29 meeting have risen from roughly 12% a week ago to somewhere between 38% and 46.5%, depending on the source, as oil prices pushed toward multi-week highs on Iran-related supply fears and reignited energy-driven inflation concerns.
signals.watch: Any fresh inflation data or Fed commentary before the meeting, and whether oil prices continue climbing on geopolitical risk.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — a binary policy event just days away could move markets sharply in either direction.

signals.title: Korea-led memory chip selloff spreads to U.S. names
signals.body: An overnight KOSPI selloff led by SK Hynix and Samsung (both down roughly 6%) spread to U.S. memory names, with Micron falling nearly 7% and SanDisk dropping 8-9%. Morgan Stanley reportedly flagged concerns about the sustainability of the AI-driven memory rally, and a Susquehanna analyst cut SanDisk's price target after identifying model errors that had overstated revenue estimates.
signals.watch: Whether the selloff extends into next week, and whether other memory-adjacent names (Western Digital, Lam Research) follow the same pattern.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — this is a specific, sourced catalyst (Korea market weakness plus an analyst model correction) rather than vague sentiment.

signals.title: Arm falls 8% despite record earnings on supply-constraint concerns
signals.body: Arm posted record quarterly earnings (60 cents per share vs. 58 cents expected, on $1.49B in revenue), but shares still fell about 8% as management pointed to memory-chip supply constraints weighing on smartphone volumes and declined to raise full-year revenue guidance despite the beat. Some of the move also reflects profit-taking after the stock's roughly 179% year-to-date gain.
signals.watch: Arm's next earnings report on July 29, and whether supply constraints ease or worsen through the rest of the year.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — a beat-but-sell-off reaction like this usually reflects a specific, identifiable concern rather than broad risk-off.

signals.title: Nasdaq closes a third straight losing session on capex and geopolitical worries
signals.body: The Nasdaq Composite has now fallen for three consecutive sessions to a one-month low, with the post-earnings hangover from Alphabet and Tesla's capex guidance compounding the memory-chip selloff and added pressure from U.S.-Iran tensions. Oracle has been especially weak, down roughly 9% over two sessions as it works through the same AI-capex-return debate as its megacap peers.
signals.watch: Whether next week's earnings reports from other AI-infrastructure names show similar capex-versus-returns friction, and how oil/Iran headlines evolve.
signals.focus: Lower conviction right now — multiple overlapping catalysts (capex skepticism, memory selloff, geopolitical risk) make it hard to isolate a single durable signal.

signals.title: Salesforce and ServiceNow bounce back while Adobe keeps sliding
signals.body: Salesforce and ServiceNow both rebounded today after Morgan Stanley's downgrade-driven selloff earlier in the week, while Adobe continued to slide following the same note's Underweight downgrade and $240 price-target cut, which cited a freemium pivot, a leadership transition, and AI-spending pressure on margins.
signals.watch: Whether Salesforce and ServiceNow's bounce holds into next week, and whether Adobe sees any analyst pushback on the downgrade.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — the divergence between the two downgraded names is now showing up clearly in price action.

signals.title: Humanoid-robotics supply chain keeps scaling globally even as individual stocks lag
signals.body: China's humanoid-robot buildout continues to move from concept to scale — Deutsche Bank flagged the sector's global acceleration, and peer Agibot reportedly reached 15,000 units produced by June. Even so, UBTECH shares remain weak, down double digits over the past month, and Tesla's Optimus narrative is still working through post-earnings timeline questions and new competitive pressure from OpenAI's robotics division.
signals.watch: Whether production and order data from Chinese humanoid makers keeps accelerating, and whether that eventually shows up in UBTECH's share price.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — the underlying scaling trend looks more durable than any single stock's day-to-day move.

signals.title: Bitcoin holds near $65K while Ether underperforms
signals.body: Bitcoin is holding close to $65,000, down less than 1.5% even as an roughly $800B AI-driven equity selloff has rattled broader risk assets, and options markets have built up nearly $5B in open interest on $70,000-$72,000 call strikes on Deribit. Ethereum has underperformed, falling further after a CPI-driven rally ran into resistance, with leveraged long liquidations adding to the pullback.
signals.watch: Whether Bitcoin's relative resilience continues if equity volatility picks up further, and whether the bullish options positioning gets tested.
signals.focus: Worth a closer look — Bitcoin's decoupling from the equity selloff is a notable divergence worth tracking, though it's still early to call it a trend.
